title: Coherent tensor-model and RHom comparisons under restriction
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, and assume chosen derived categories of module sheaves on X, on each over-site over an open of X, and on U [def-pc-derived-category], all in the same localization universe. Fix A in D(O_X), a K-flat integer-indexed complex P [def-pc-kflat-complex], and an isomorphism e_A:Q(P)≅A. Let R be derived open restriction followed by the canonical over-site equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Put B_J=Q(Tot(P tensor J)) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], H_E=RHom_X(A,E) and H_U(E)=RHom_U(R(A),R(E)) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write e_X and e_U for the fixed canonical tensor-Hom equivalences [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection]. There are simultaneous families of isomorphisms c_J:B_J≅Q(J) tensor A, d_J:R(B_J)≅R(Q(J)) tensor R(A), and h_E:R(H_E)≅H_U(E), such that for every chain map u:J→J', R(Q(id_P tensor u));d_J'.hom=d_J.hom;(R(Q(u)) tensor id_R(A)); and for every derived morphism ξ:Q(J)→H_E, d_J.hom;e_U(R(ξ);h_E.hom)=R(c_J.hom;e_X(ξ)). Neither K-flatness of J nor any boundedness or augmentation is assumed.

proof.text: Use the K-flat localization tensor comparison on P and the identity family of arbitrary complexes J. Invert its components, apply e_A on the first tensor factor, and then the derived tensor symmetry; this gives c_J with order Q(J) tensor A. Restrict P, which remains K-flat, and use the total-tensor restriction comparison and the localization factorization of R to give d_J. Take these particular natural comparisons; their naturality gives R(Q(id_P tensor u));d_J'.hom=d_J.hom;(R(Q(u)) tensor id).

Compute RHom with the fixed functorial K-injective representative I of E. Open restriction preserves K-injectivity. The termwise Hom restriction comparison and the canonical over-site equivalence identify R(H_E) with RHom_U(R(A),R(E)), defining h_E. Use the same resolution and localization comparisons in c, d and h, rather than unrelated object isomorphisms.

The canonical tensor-Hom family is specified by uncurrying on each total-tensor summand. Restriction of that local linear map is precisely uncurrying of its restriction; the tensor, Hom and resolution comparisons above identify the source and target. Thus d_J.hom;e_U(R(ξ);h_E.hom)=R(c_J.hom;e_X(ξ)) for chain representatives. Because P is K-flat, Hom(P,I) is K-injective; restriction remains K-injective. Derived morphisms from arbitrary Q(J) into this object are represented by chain maps modulo homotopy. Uncurrying preserves homotopies, hence the equality holds for every ξ, with no K-flatness of J. For the zero complex and empty open the same component equations hold.

theorem exists_tensorModel_restriction_comparisons
    (X : Scheme.{uX}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (A : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlat (R := X.sheaf) P)
    (eA : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ A) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    letI := (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed X.sheaf).1.some
    let R := ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
      Equivalence.functor
        (C := SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (D := SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
        (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let H := fun E ↦ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
      X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op A, E)
    let B := fun J ↦ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P J (curriedTensor _))
    let HU := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)
      U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    ∃ (c : ∀ J, B J ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj J ⊗ A)
      (d : ∀ J, R.obj (B J) ≅ R.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J) ⊗ R.obj A)
      (h : ∀ E, R.obj (H E) ≅ HU.obj (op (R.obj A), R.obj E)),
      (∀ J J' (u : J ⟶ J'),
        R.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMap (𝟙 P) u (curriedTensor _)
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) ≫ (d J').hom =
          (d J).hom ≫ (R.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map u) ⊗ₘ 𝟙 (R.obj A))) ∧
      (∀ J E (ξ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj J ⟶ H E),
        (d J).hom ≫ schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv U.toScheme
          (R.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J)) (R.obj A) (R.obj E)
          (R.map ξ ≫ (h E).hom) =
        R.map ((c J).hom ≫ schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J) A E ξ))
